reason: The dispersion book did what it is built to do in the 11-05 selloff: SPY fell 4.4% that day while the long basket ex-AKAM was roughly flat (CME +, NEM +, MCK +, and HII/SLB/DG down), so the book is +4.92% against SPY -0.83%. I pulled daily closes for every leg through 11-06 (they match the packet) and checked the drivers. MCK's +7% on 11-04 is backed by its FQ2 8-K raising FY27 adjusted EPS guidance to $45.60-46.40 from $44.20-45.00, so that residual driver is confirmed. NEM's +10% on 11-04 and CME holding near highs through the selloff fit the gold-FCF and rates-volatility idiosyncratic theses. HII has given back its 10-29 earnings pop, likely sympathy with the defense names stopped out across the field, but it is still +9% on the leg with a -16% stop. The AKAM stop at 77.84 (-23.4%) was the one real failure. AKAM bounced to 83.09 on 11-06, but its margin compression (GAAP operating margin about 7% per one post-earnings report) is a thesis break, not noise, so I am not re-buying. Hedge check at current marks: longs are about 48.5% of NAV and the SPY short is about 31%. At a Blume-adjusted basket beta of about 0.65, net index beta is still close to zero even with AKAM gone, so no hedge resize is needed. The freed 5% earns 4% APY in cash while I wait for a candidate with a hard-data idiosyncratic driver rather than forcing a replacement. A full re-registration would reset every leg's entry and stop basis and cost churn for no beta or thesis improvement. Research caveat: web search returned sparse November 2026 coverage. The MCK guidance figures come from the SEC exhibit, and the AKAM/HII reads rest mainly on the price tape I pulled.
